rationale: Construction step for the open sweep gap (984747de5ed94b4ea8f6977b2a92808f-gap-2): the sweep case in the fixed harness now also proposes configuration changes and, unlike the previous revision, applies them the way an application must. Each iteration adds a case that builds a ConfChangeV2 with a single change (AddLearnerNode, AddNode or RemoveNode for node 4) and proposes it on the current leader through confChangeToMsg/MsgProp, and the persist/apply step now hands every committed EntryConfChangeV2 to nodes[id].applyConfChange after unmarshalling it, so the node's tracked configuration actually changes rather than only its applied index. Two construction facts are worth recording because they cost real iterations: the first draft panicked inside the repository's network helper (raft_test.go:4117 dereferenced a missing state machine) as soon as a leader sent a message to the newly configured node 4, which shows the network helper has no state machine for an id that exists only in the configuration; registering the package's own black-hole stepper for id 4 makes those messages drop instead, after which the case runs. The draft-side run now reports invariant_sweep_summary with seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=467, ordinary proposals=452, conf_change_proposals=317 and violations=0, i.e. the four invariants still show no counterexample with configuration changes in the event set. Restarts from persisted storage are still absent, so the gap is only partially addressed; the experiment below requests a fresh isolated execution of the extended harness so the configuration-change half is receipt-backed rather than draft-side.

scope.description: Fourth revision of the same fixed harness. Probes A, B and C are unchanged. The sweep case (TestAssuranceInvariantSweep) now includes configuration events: with the same probability mass as ordinary proposals it builds a ConfChangeV2 with one change on node 4 (AddLearnerNode, AddNode or RemoveNode) and proposes it on the current leader via confChangeToMsg/MsgProp; the persist/apply step passes every committed EntryConfChangeV2 to nodes[id].applyConfChange before advancing, so the tracked configuration changes; and a black-hole state machine is registered for id 4 so the network helper drops messages addressed to a node that exists only in the configuration instead of dereferencing nil. The four invariants (at most one leader per term, no committed index ever observed with a different term, committed-index monotonicity, applied <= committed) are checked after every event, and the run ends with invariant_sweep_summary reporting seeds, steps, elections, ordinary proposals, conf_change_proposals and violations. Node restarts from persisted storage are deliberately not part of this revision.
assumptions: All events, storage and transport come from the snapshot's own test facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange); no production logic is modified.

Only node 4 is ever added or removed by configuration events, and all three operations are safe to apply repeatedly, so the configuration cannot be driven into an invalid transition by the random sequence.
Node 4 is represented by the package's own black-hole stepper, i.e. a configured participant that never responds; committed decisions therefore still need the original voters.
Randomness is fixed per seed, and absence of violations over this event set is a holds-only result rather than a safety proof.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..3 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), wrap them with newNetwork and register nopStepper for id 4; then for 60 steps pick one of MsgHup on a random node, MsgProp with a tagged payload, tick() on a random node, isolate a random node, recover, TransferLeader from a random voter to the current leader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (AddLearnerNode/AddNode/RemoveNode for node 4), or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply all nodes - applying committed conf changes through applyConfChange - and evaluate the four invariants, emitting a violation event with seed, step, nodes and operands when one is found, and finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation as the previous sweep execution, with the configuration-change half of the open gap now built: the harness adds a ConfChangeV2 proposal event and applies committed conf changes through applyConfChange, plus a black-hole peer for the configured-but-absent node 4. Probes A-C are unchanged. Fresh execution is required because the harness bytes and the event set changed.
